chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Zihar is of two types: one in which the expiation is before consummation, and the other after. The one that requires expiation before consummation is the one who says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and does not say, 'If I do such and such to you.' And the one that requires expiation after consummation is the one who says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother if I approach you.'

key_terms.أُمِّي: My mother (used in the formulaic comparison of Zihar)
key_terms.الظَّهَارُ: Zihar, a form of irrevocable divorce where a husband compares his wife to his mother's back
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation required to rectify the Zihar

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Zihar before and after consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between definitive and conditional Zihar based on whether the declaration precedes or follows sexual consummation, a nuance critical for determining the specific expiation (Kaffarah) required. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic conditions in marital law, linking the timing of the oath to the obligation of freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor as detailed in the Quran.
